statement.p:
You have 8 presents to give to your 4 kids. How many ways can this be done if:
The presents are identical, and each kid gets at least one present?
The presents are identical, and some kids might get no presents?
The presents are unique, and some kids might get no presents?
The presents are unique and each kid gets at least one present?

li.p: {7 \choose 4} ways. After giving one present to each kid, you are left with 4 presents (stones) which need to be divided among the 4 kids (giving 3 sticks).
{11 \choose 8}={165} ways. You have 8 stones and 3 sticks.
4^{8}\text{.} You have 4 choices for whom to give each present. This is like making a function from the set of presents to the set of kids.
4^{8}- \left[{4 \choose 1}(4-1)^{8} - {4\choose 2}(4-2)^{8} + {4 \choose 3}(4-3)^{8} \dots \right] ways. Now the function from the set of presents to the set of kids must be surjective.
